claims.claim: The same organisation reports that the detector works well on plain prose but is sometimes tripped up by formatting, markup and non-prose text.

claims.claim: Chambers and Kelley measured that 1.7 percent of all 59,947 Reddit posts in their corpus were flagged as AI-generated by the OpenAI GPT-2 detector.
claims.source: Summer Chambers & Matthew C. Kelley, 'The Misclassification of Autistic Writing as AI-Generated'
claims.quote: 1.7% of all 59,947 posts were flagged by the model as AI-generated

claims.claim: In the same experiment posts from the likely-autistic subcorpus had a twenty-five percent greater chance of being classified as AI-generated.
claims.quote: posts from the likely-autistic subcorpus had a 25% greater chance

claims.claim: In the follow-up experiment on posts truncated to exactly three hundred words the gap widened, with likely-autistic posts having a fifty percent greater chance of being classified as AI-generated.
claims.quote: posts from the likely-autistic subcorpus had a 50% greater chance

claims.claim: The same paper reports that less than two percent of either subcorpus was flagged as AI-generated, so the disproportion sits inside a very low absolute flagging rate.
claims.quote: less than two-percent of either subcorpus was flagged as AI-generated

claims.claim: The same study measured that GPT-4o uses nominalizations 2.1 times as often as humans.

claims.claim: The same study found that the Llama base models use these distinguishing features at rates more closely matching humans than the instruction-tuned models do.

claims.page: Results, comparison of base and instruction-tuned models
